input.title: From Accra Sundays Outward

picks.why: Start where your parents did: highlife brass and guitar, the Sunday-afternoon dance music of Accra.
Hear highlife's next life, folded into bright Afrobeats drums built for West African street parties.
A diaspora sound mixing the music of home with the music of where you live now.
American hip-hop, one of the threads Afrobeats and afro-fusion weave back in, closing the loop toward your other home.
A South African cousin showing how African dance music keeps traveling, from township parties to dance floors worldwide.

input.story: Ama Serwaa Band plays the brass-and-guitar highlife that reconnects diaspora-curious listeners with their elders' dance music. That sound didn't stay still: Afrobeats took shape in Ghana and Nigeria by mixing highlife with hip-hop, dancehall and R&B, then reached global charts with help from diaspora scenes. Afro-fusion goes further, blending home rhythms with the music of where artists live now. Meanwhile amapiano, born in South Africa's townships, shows the continent's dance music spreading worldwide on its own path.
